claims.text: The initial alloy is equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi.
The initial CoCrFeMnNi alloy is homogeneous and single phase.
The initial homogeneous CoCrFeMnNi alloy has high toughness and ductile behavior.
High configurational entropy stabilizes the initial single-phase structure.
Cyclic loading produces localized plastic deformation along activated slip bands.
Localized plastic deformation along slip bands reduces the local mixing entropy.
The proposed reduction in local mixing entropy triggers nanoscale solute segregation.
The proposed reduction in local mixing entropy triggers incipient nanoscale phase separation or precipitation.
The nanoscale solute clusters or precipitates form preferentially along activated slip bands within grain interiors rather than along grain boundaries.
Combined aging at 500–600 °C for up to 100 hours and high-cycle fatigue promotes more nanoscale precipitation than thermal aging alone.
The deformation-induced nanoscale precipitates act as internal stress concentrators.
The deformation-induced nanoscale precipitates serve as nucleation sites for brittle fracture.
The formation of nanoscale precipitates along slip bands decreases fracture toughness.
Combined thermal aging and cyclic loading causes earlier crack initiation than in the initial or thermal-aging-only baseline.
Brittle behavior emerges only above a threshold cyclic strain amplitude and accumulated time-temperature product.
Below the proposed service thresholds, the alloy retains favorable toughness.
The proposed brittle behavior is an intragranular, deformation-induced process distinct from grain-boundary embrittlement.
Embrittlement in conventional alloys is predominantly associated with grain-boundary phenomena.
